page.layout: One printed page. Full-width running head at top with page number left. Title block centred beneath (heading). Central engraving in a framed box (not text). Below the engraving, a four-line verse centred in italic. At lower right, a catchword-like word "Omnes" set off to the right.

main_text.head: GNOMON, TYPVSQVE VITÆ Christianæ.
main_text.p: [engraving: emblem of a globe with crown and arms, holding a mace and a serpent-entwined cross, a Decalogus tablet and an hourglass below, hands pointing from the sides, and a bird at upper left; described under notes]
main_text.l: Vt præsens sine labe queas transmittere seclum,
Vtq; homini possis gratus & esse Deo:

page.notes: The engraving shows a globe wearing a crown, held between two arms; a mace with a bird perched on it at left, a serpent coiled around a cross at right; a tablet labelled "Decalogus" in the centre; an hourglass with ribbon beneath; hands pointing in from both sides; hills at the base. The verse lines are set in italic. "Ruštantes" is read as printed; the long s and š-like letter may be a misreading of "Ruffantes" and is marked uncertain. The word "Omnes" at lower right is a printed catchword-like word set apart; it is placed in main text as a short line, its status is uncertain.
